hint: Kings once ruled from here. Today, people in rented silk walk the same stone courtyards.
reveal: The largest of Seoul's five grand palaces, built in 1395 as the main royal seat of the Joseon dynasty.
tip: Wearing hanbok gets you in free. Catch the guard-changing ceremony at the main gate.

approach.clue: Walk north through the big square toward the mountain. Pass both statues; the gate at the end, guarded by people in bright uniforms, is your stop.

hint: A royal residence that bends to the hills instead of flattening them, with a garden kings kept for themselves.
reveal: A UNESCO World Heritage palace famous for harmonizing architecture with the natural landscape.
tip: The Secret Garden (Huwon) tour needs a separate ticket; book ahead.

approach.clue: Walk east along the main road for about 5 minutes. The old wooden gate on your left is where you're going.

hint: Curved tile roofs line narrow alleys where people still live. Speak softly here.
reveal: A 600-year-old residential neighborhood of traditional Korean houses (hanok) between two palaces.
tip: Real residents live here; visiting hours are limited and quiet is expected.

approach.clue: Walk uphill (north) from the station for 5–10 minutes. When the rooftops start to curve, slip into the quiet side alleys.

hint: Even the global coffee chains here write their signs in the local alphabet.
reveal: Seoul's street of traditional crafts, tea houses and galleries.
tip: Look for Ssamziegil, a spiral-shaped craft mall, and try a traditional tea house.

approach.clue: Find the street sloping gently south, lined with tea houses and craft shops. You'll know it by the signs written only in Korean.

hint: Hundred-year-old houses, brand-new desserts. Old roofs, young crowds.
reveal: A maze of 1920s hanok converted into cafes, bakeries and small restaurants.
tip: Weekday afternoons are far less crowded.

hint: Couples leave something locked up here, and the whole city lies at your feet.
reveal: The iconic tower on Namsan mountain with 360-degree views of Seoul.
tip: Take the Namsan cable car or the free-flowing yellow bus 01A. Best at sunset.

approach.clue: Look up and head for the tallest thing on the hill. Walk uphill toward the mountain; a cable car can carry you most of the way.

hint: Skincare samples in one hand, a skewer of something sizzling in the other.
reveal: Seoul's busiest shopping street, famous for K-beauty stores and evening street food.
tip: Street food stalls open around 4-5 PM.

hint: Over a century of sizzling pancakes and noodles. Grab a stool and point at what looks good.
reveal: One of Korea's oldest traditional markets (1905), a legend for street food.
tip: Try bindaetteok (mung bean pancake) and mayak gimbap.

approach.clue: Follow your nose: the entrance is steps from the station. Walk in toward the sizzling griddles in the middle.

hint: A river once buried under a highway, now running below the skyscrapers again.
reveal: A restored urban stream running 11 km through downtown Seoul.
tip: Walk east from the plaza; it's lit up beautifully after dark.

approach.clue: Head a few minutes east to a plaza with a giant spiral sculpture. The steps behind it lead down to the water.

hint: It looks like a silver spaceship that landed in a fashion district. There are no straight lines.
reveal: Zaha Hadid's futuristic landmark, surrounded by 24-hour fashion markets.
tip: At night, check the LED rose garden and the building's light projections.

hint: 123 floors up. The floor under your feet might be glass.
reveal: Korea's tallest building (555 m), with an observatory and a glass-floor sky deck.
tip: Go about an hour before sunset to see both day and night views.

approach.clue: Look up. You can't miss the tallest building in Korea.

hint: A lake walk where a giant tower and a fairy-tale castle share the reflection.
reveal: A lakeside loop trail beside Lotte World, loved by locals for slow walks.
tip: The 2.5 km loop takes about 40 minutes at an easy pace.

approach.clue: Walk toward the water beside the theme park and start the loop.

hint: Monks chant here, 1,200 years in the making, while glass towers watch from across the road.
reveal: A Buddhist temple founded in 794, sitting right in the middle of Gangnam.
tip: Look for the giant stone Maitreya Buddha. Temple-stay programs are available.

hint: Bookshelves taller than houses, in the middle of a shopping mall. Yes, you can read them.
reveal: A free public library with 13 m-high bookshelves inside COEX Mall.
tip: It's free. Grab a seat upstairs for the best photo angle.

approach.clue: Go into the huge mall connected to the station and head for its center. When the ceiling suddenly soars, look up.

hint: A giant wave crashes against the glass, but nobody gets wet.
reveal: Home of Korea's largest outdoor LED screen, famous for its 3D wave illusion.
tip: Stand across the street near the intersection for the full 3D effect.

approach.clue: Come up at the big intersection by the convention center and watch the giant screen on the corner building.

hint: Old shoe factories turned into the coolest cafes in the city. Pop-up stores come and go weekly.
reveal: Seoul's 'Brooklyn', full of warehouse cafes, designer shops and brand pop-ups.
tip: Check what pop-up stores are open this week; many are free to enter.

hint: Deer, forest trails and picnic lawns, next to high-rise apartments.
reveal: A large urban park by the Han River, formerly a racetrack and water purification site.
tip: Visit the deer enclosure and the insect botanical garden.

approach.clue: The green entrance is right by the station. Walk in and keep an eye out for deer.

hint: Order fried chicken to a patch of grass by the river. Locals really do this.
reveal: The most popular Han River park, famous for picnics and riverside delivery food.
tip: Try instant ramen from the convenience store machine by the river.

hint: A bridge that dances. Rainbow water falls from it, set to music.
reveal: A Guinness-record bridge fountain on the Han River with music and light shows.
tip: Night shows (roughly 19:30-21:00, April-October) are the most beautiful.

hint: Hillside stairs painted by artists. The walls tell stories if you climb.
reveal: A hillside neighborhood decorated with murals and art installations.
tip: It is a residential area; keep your voice down.

approach.clue: Take exit 2, walk through the small park, then keep going uphill. Follow the stairs that someone decided to paint.

hint: Walk along a 600-year-old wall as the city lights come on below.
reveal: A hilltop park along the Joseon-era fortress wall with night views of Seoul.
tip: The wall trail is softly lit at night and one of Seoul's best free viewpoints.

approach.clue: Keep climbing past the painted walls until you meet an old stone wall. Walk along it.

hint: A royal palace where a Western-style stone hall stands beside wooden pavilions.
reveal: A palace in downtown Seoul mixing Joseon and early-1900s Western architecture.
tip: Walk the stone-wall road (Deoksugung Doldam-gil) outside afterward.

approach.clue: Come up by the big lawn in front of City Hall. The palace gate with guards is right across the road.

hint: An old overpass that cars forgot. Now it grows trees.
reveal: A former highway overpass turned into an elevated walkway garden.
tip: Nice at night, with views of the old Seoul Station building.

hint: A department store with an indoor forest and a waterfall under a glass roof.
reveal: Seoul's biggest department store, known for its indoor garden and trendy pop-ups.
tip: The basement food hall is one of the best in the city.

hint: A neighborhood market where a croquette costs less than a coffee.
reveal: A local traditional market near Hongdae, beloved for cheap and tasty snacks.
tip: Grab snacks here and eat them by the Han River at nearby Mangwon Hangang Park.

hint: Trains used to run here. Now people lie on the grass with coffee.
reveal: A linear park built on an old railway, lined with cafes in Yeonnam-dong.
tip: Locals nicknamed it after New York's Central Park.

hint: Dance crews and street musicians compete for crowds every evening.
reveal: The heart of Seoul's youth, indie music and K-pop street dance culture.
tip: Busking peaks on weekend evenings.

hint: Five old houses moved here from across the city, with a time capsule buried for 400 years.
reveal: A free hanok village at the foot of Namsan with traditional games and crafts.
tip: Free entry. Try traditional games like tuho (arrow throwing).

hint: Planes and tanks rest outside; inside, the story of a divided peninsula.
reveal: A massive museum about Korea's military history, especially the Korean War.
tip: Free entry. The outdoor exhibition of aircraft is great for photos.

hint: A 'room of quiet contemplation' holds two smiling figures deep in thought.
reveal: Korea's largest museum, home to national treasures across 5,000 years.
tip: Free entry. Don't miss the Room of Quiet Contemplation with two pensive bodhisattvas.

hint: A giant golden king sits here, next to the admiral who beat a navy with a handful of ships.
reveal: Seoul's central plaza with statues of King Sejong and Admiral Yi Sun-sin.
tip: Walk beneath King Sejong's statue to find a free exhibition hall.

hint: Hundreds of lanterns hang overhead in the middle of downtown traffic.
reveal: The chief temple of Korea's largest Buddhist order, right in central Seoul.
tip: The lanterns are most spectacular around Buddha's Birthday in spring.

approach.clue: Walk a few minutes south-west. Follow the sound of chanting and look for lanterns hanging over a courtyard.

hint: Climb aboard and let the city scroll past your window for an hour and a half. Hop off anywhere, or ride the whole loop.
reveal: The hop-on hop-off tour bus from Gwanghwamun, looping past palaces, Myeongdong, DDP and Insadong in about 90 minutes.
tip: Buses leave every 40 minutes (09:30-17:00). Buy tickets at the booth near Gwanghwamun Station exit 6. No service on Mondays.

hint: One departure only, as the sun goes down. Take a seat up high and watch the bridges light up one by one.
reveal: A one-hour evening bus tour from Gwanghwamun past lit-up Han River bridges and downtown night views.
tip: Departs around 19:00 in September (18:30 in October). Arrive 30 minutes early at the Gwanghwamun booth. No service on Mondays.

hint: Leave the streets behind. For the next hour, you'll see the city from the water.
reveal: The Han River ferry cruise from Yeouido, with daytime, sunset, moonlight-music and starlight sailings.
tip: Weekday sailings around 14:00-16:00, sunset at 18:00, moonlight music cruises at 19:00 and 20:20. Arrive 20 minutes early.

hint: Time for a costume change. Flowing silk, bright colors, and a hairpin to finish the look.
reveal: Dozens of hanbok (traditional Korean clothing) rental shops cluster around Gyeongbokgung Station.
tip: Rentals start around 15,000-30,000 won for a few hours. Wearing hanbok gets you into the royal palaces for free.

approach.clue: Look around the station exits for shop windows full of colorful silk dresses.

hint: A small cabin will lift you off the ground and carry you up a mountain, right from downtown.
reveal: Since 1962, this cable car has carried visitors up Namsan mountain to the foot of N Seoul Tower.
tip: Lines get long at sunset. Buy a round-trip ticket, or walk down the forest trail afterward.

approach.clue: Walk uphill toward the mountain and follow the signs with a little cabin on them.

hint: Roller coasters under a glass dome, and a fairy-tale castle on an island. Scream as loud as you like.
reveal: One of the world's largest indoor theme parks, with an outdoor Magic Island by Seokchon Lake.
tip: Afternoon 'After 4' tickets are cheaper. Wearing a school-uniform rental is a local tradition here.

approach.clue: Everything is connected underground. Follow the signs from the station into the big complex.

hint: Two wheels, a river breeze, and a public bike you unlock with your phone. Pedal as far as you like.
reveal: Ttukseom Hangang Park, where Seoul's public bikes (Ttareungyi) and riverside paths meet.
tip: The Seoul Bike (Ttareungyi) app has an English mode; a 1-hour pass costs about 1,000 won.

hint: A tiny soundproof booth, two microphones, and a screen full of K-pop. Your high notes are safe here.
reveal: Coin noraebang: pay-per-song karaoke booths, a favorite pastime of Korean students around Hongdae.
tip: Songs cost about 500 won each. Most machines have an English search option.

hint: A whole young chicken stuffed with rice and ginseng, bubbling in a stone pot. Locals queue for this even in summer.
reveal: A legendary samgyetang (ginseng chicken soup) restaurant in a traditional hanok near Gyeongbokgung.
tip: Expect a queue at lunch, but it moves fast. A small glass of ginseng liquor comes with your soup.

approach.clue: Take exit 2 and walk a couple of minutes down the side street. Look for a line of people outside a traditional house.

hint: Silky knife-cut noodles in a rich broth, and kimchi so garlicky it's famous on its own. Refills are free.
reveal: Serving kalguksu (knife-cut noodle soup) and dumplings in the heart of Seoul's shopping district since 1966.
tip: Order kalguksu and mandu. You pay upfront, and noodle refills are free.

approach.clue: Dive into the shopping streets and look for a fast-moving queue. Noodles here arrive in minutes.

hint: A whole chicken arrives in a giant pot at your table. When it's gone, the noodles go in.
reveal: The original 'dakhanmari' (one-whole-chicken hot pot) restaurant, tucked into an alley near Dongdaemun for decades.
tip: Mix your own dipping sauce with chili paste, mustard, soy and vinegar. Add kalguksu noodles at the end.

hint: A bowl of milky, gentle broth and plump hand-made dumplings, a short walk from old tiled roofs.
reveal: A beloved noodle house near Bukchon, known for its beef-bone kalguksu and large dumplings.
tip: Try the noodle and dumpling combo. Lines are shortest right at opening.

approach.clue: Walk north toward the hills and watch the side streets for a queue outside a noodle house.

hint: Cold, chewy buckwheat noodles in an icy beef broth, from a recipe carried south decades ago.
reveal: One of Seoul's oldest restaurants (since 1946), famous for Pyongyang-style naengmyeon and bulgogi.
tip: Order the mul-naengmyeon and taste the subtle broth before adding vinegar or mustard. Closed on Mondays.

hint: Marinated beef ribs sizzle at your table while a waterfall runs through the garden outside.
reveal: A Gangnam institution since 1976 for premium Korean BBQ (galbi), built around a traditional garden.
tip: Yangnyeom galbi (marinated ribs) is the classic order. Pricey, but a local special-occasion favorite.

hint: Sit on a wooden floor in a century-old house, with bread buried under a snowfall of powdered sugar.
reveal: A hanok cafe near Anguk Station, famous for its pandoro bread and courtyard seating.
tip: Go early on weekends; the pandoro sells out.

approach.clue: It's almost next to the station: look for a hanok courtyard full of people holding pastries.

hint: Coffee among raw concrete and crumbling brick, in a building that once did very different work.
reveal: The original Onion cafe, a converted industrial building in Seongsu with a famous bakery counter.
tip: Grab the pandoro and an Americano and sit on the rooftop-style upper floor.

hint: A giant old warehouse where art hangs from the rafters and people sip lattes underneath.
reveal: A former rice-mill warehouse turned gallery cafe, the building that kicked off Seongsu's cafe boom.
tip: Admission is usually covered by your drink order.

hint: A retro-style bakery cafe with a seal for a mascot, where the best bread disappears before noon.
reveal: One of Seoul's best-loved specialty coffee roasters, with vintage Korean design near Gongdeok.
tip: Pair a hand-drip coffee with a croissant or whatever seasonal bread is fresh.

hint: A clear, golden beef broth that has barely changed since the 1930s. When today's pot runs out, the doors close.
reveal: A historic gomtang (beef bone soup) house in Myeongdong, a Blue Ribbon and Michelin-listed classic.
tip: Open 07:00-16:00 and closes early when sold out. Closed on Sundays.

hint: A tree-lined street where designer boutiques hide in the side alleys, and the side alleys are the real prize.
reveal: Sinsa-dong's ginkgo-lined boulevard of fashion flagships, concept stores and cafés.
tip: Explore the parallel back streets (Serosu-gil) for independent shops.

hint: Korea's oldest and busiest market maze: glasses, ginseng, kitchenware and hotteok all in one block.
reveal: A 600-year-old traditional market beside the Sungnyemun gate, with over 10,000 shops.
tip: Try the vegetable japchae hotteok near the main alley; many shops close on Sundays.

hint: Steep streets, rooftop bars and a dozen languages on every corner. A drama made this neighborhood a pilgrimage.
reveal: Seoul's most international neighborhood, made famous worldwide by the drama Itaewon Class.
tip: Walk up to the Gyeongnidan-gil side streets for rooftop views at sunset.
